editorial_thesis: Useful AI progress is moving into operating systems for work: routing and budgets, guided production, evidence-bearing research, and identity interfaces that make capability governable.

topic_groups.title: Enterprise Agent Operations
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Fresh enterprise case studies move the conversation from “can agents help?” to operating design: model routing, ontologies, budgets, accountability, and repeatable deployment.

sources.title: LegalOn halves Codex costs while maintaining development speed
sources.why_selected: AID CoE, task-based model routing, Fast-mode exceptions, and tiered budgets reportedly cut estimated daily costs about 65% while preserving development speed.
sources.usefulness: Use a lightweight-first routing policy, reserve frontier modes for architecture and orchestration, and give new initiatives more budget than mature workflows.

sources.title: How Oracle turns days of work into minutes with ChatGPT and Codex
sources.why_selected: Oracle combines business ontologies, natural-language requests, Codex, and human review across recruiting, analytics, operations, and incident response.
sources.usefulness: The reusable pattern is outcome intake → governed system access → checked output, not a generic chatbot bolted onto a database.

sources.title: Google Cloud introduces the Gemini agent
sources.why_selected: Google Cloud positions a universal work agent around business context, skills, tools, model choice, cost controls, and enterprise governance.
sources.usefulness: Treat the prompt window as an orchestration surface over existing documents, inboxes, and developer environments.

sources.title: Barclays scales Claude to upgrade operations
sources.why_selected: A large bank is extending Claude across software development, legacy modernization, and operational work.
sources.usefulness: Enterprise adoption is becoming portfolio management: prioritize repeatable high-friction work, then measure throughput and quality.

sources.title: Claude Frontier Academy
sources.why_selected: Anthropic announced a $100M program to train 10,000 engineers, signaling that agent deployment capacity is becoming a labor and enablement constraint.
sources.usefulness: Buildn can package agent literacy as operating practice: task selection, review, cost, and failure handling.

topic_groups.title: Creative Production Systems
topic_groups.selection_rationale: A neglected lane earns inclusion because current tools are making orchestration, templates, and distribution—not raw generation—the practical creative leverage point.

sources.title: Pollo AI turns creative ideas into campaigns with OpenAI
sources.why_selected: Pollo Agent turns rough ideas and product photos into storylines, scenes, images, and short campaign videos, using different models for routing, reasoning, and image generation.
sources.usefulness: A Buildn/client offer could standardize campaign briefs, variant generation, and approval evidence while leaving model choice behind the scenes.

sources.title: Playground: Create and Play Custom Games
sources.why_selected: Google Playground lets users create, remix, play, and share browser games from natural-language prompts, with community discovery and a possible path into Unity.
sources.usefulness: It is a useful reference for “prompt to artifact” UX: immediate feedback, remixability, sharing, and progressive depth.

sources.title: Autodesk advances AI for design and manufacturing
sources.why_selected: Autodesk is applying AI across repetitive design, engineering, and manufacturing workflows rather than treating generation as a standalone feature.
sources.usefulness: Vertical workflow context is the moat: embed suggestions where constraints, files, approvals, and downstream production already exist.

sources.title: AI in Design 2026: the inflection point is here
sources.why_selected: Designer Fund reports a nuanced shift toward designers owning more and shipping more, rather than simple replacement narratives.
sources.usefulness: Use AI to widen exploration while preserving a human-owned decision record for the final direction.

sources.title: Inside our 353,000-person vibe coding course
sources.why_selected: Google describes a large-scale program for learning agent-assisted building, a signal that creative production and lightweight software creation are converging.
sources.usefulness: Client prototyping can become a structured service: prompt, test, critique, and harden—not one-shot vibe coding.

topic_groups.title: Proof-Carrying AI Research
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Research transparency and formal verification are under-covered relative to product launches, yet they offer a concrete pattern for trustworthy AI outputs.

sources.title: Sharing AI progress in mathematics
sources.why_selected: OpenAI released AI-produced mathematical results with citations, revision protocols, Lean formalizations, reasoning summaries, compute estimates, and attempt statistics.
sources.usefulness: Buildn reports can attach provenance, supporting evidence, revision history, and machine-checkable artifacts to recommendations.

sources.title: OpenAI mathematics repository
sources.why_selected: The accompanying repository is the concrete artifact surface for papers, formalizations, and release updates.
sources.usefulness: Repositories make research outputs inspectable, forkable, and auditable instead of trapping them in a polished page.

sources.title: Advisory Group on Mathematics and AI
sources.why_selected: The advisory group publishes recommendations for responsible sharing of major AI-generated mathematical results.
sources.usefulness: External release guidance is a useful check against overstating novelty, hiding uncertainty, or omitting provenance.

sources.title: 2026 Knowledge Management Priorities and Trends Survey
sources.why_selected: APQC’s survey offers current evidence about where knowledge-management teams are directing effort and attention.
sources.usefulness: Pair AI retrieval with explicit knowledge ownership, lifecycle, and usefulness measures.

sources.title: Can we predict the jobs robots will do?
sources.why_selected: Anthropic analyzes which kinds of work may be exposed to robotic automation, linking task structure to physical-world deployment.
sources.usefulness: The task-level lens transfers to agent opportunity mapping: decompose jobs into observable, repeatable, reviewable units.

topic_groups.title: Identity + Trust Interfaces
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Identity is a coverage gap and a practical prerequisite for agentic work: secure sign-in, content provenance, and tiered access determine whether automation can be trusted.

sources.title: Sign in quickly and securely with passkeys
sources.why_selected: Google is using Cybersecurity Awareness Month to push passkeys as device-bound, phishing-resistant sign-in.
sources.usefulness: Make strong authentication the default for operator and client surfaces before adding more automation.

sources.title: We’re making it easier to identify AI-generated content
sources.why_selected: Google DeepMind describes SynthID work to identify AI-generated content across media types.
sources.usefulness: Generated artifacts should carry provenance and disclosure metadata where possible, especially in client-facing creative workflows.

sources.title: Zero-knowledge-proof library donation
sources.why_selected: Google highlights a Linux Foundation Europe effort around a more private digital world using zero-knowledge proof technology.
sources.usefulness: Privacy-preserving claims can reduce the need to expose raw identity or event data to an agent.

sources.title: Expanding the Cyber Verification Program
sources.why_selected: Anthropic’s three access tiers separate defensive work, authorized red teaming, and specialized critical-system testing.
sources.usefulness: Capability should follow identity, authorization, target scope, and review depth—not just a user’s prompt.

sources.title: Google DeepMind SynthID
sources.why_selected: SynthID provides a product-level view of watermarking and provenance across generated media.
sources.usefulness: A provenance control is more useful when it is attached to the artifact lifecycle, not added at publication time.
